skills.name: Angles on a line and around a point
skills.description: 180° on a straight line, 360° around a point.

skills.name: Angles in a triangle
skills.description: The three angles add up to 180°.

GEO_LINE_360.label: Thinks angles on a straight line add up to 360°
GEO_LINE_360.explanation: Subtracts from 360° instead of 180° on a straight line.

GEO_LINE_90.label: Subtracts from 90° instead of 180°
GEO_LINE_90.explanation: Treats a straight line like a right angle.

GEO_POINT_180.label: Thinks angles around a point add up to 180°
GEO_POINT_180.explanation: Uses the straight-line total for a full turn.

GEO_TRIANGLE_360.label: Thinks the angles in a triangle add up to 360°
GEO_TRIANGLE_360.explanation: Confuses the triangle total with a full turn.

questions.prompt: Two angles sit together on a straight line. One is 130°. What is the other, in degrees?
hints: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
Angles all the way round a point add up to 360°.
solution: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

angles_on_a_line.title: Angles on a line and around a point
angles_on_a_line.big_idea: A straight line is half a turn: the angles on it add up to 180°. A full turn around a point is 360°.
steps: Decide: is it a straight line (180°) or all the way round a point (360°)?
Add up the angles you know.
angles_on_a_line.sense_check: If one angle on a line is 130°, the other must be small, 50°. 230° would be bigger than the whole line.

worked_examples.prompt: One angle on a straight line is 130°. The other?
Around a point: 100°, 120° and x. x?

angles_in_a_triangle.title: Angles in a triangle
angles_in_a_triangle.big_idea: The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°: tear the corners off a paper triangle and they make a straight line.
steps: Add the two angles you know.
angles_in_a_triangle.sense_check: A triangle's third angle can't be more than 180°, so 250° is impossible.
